clue.text: One finds investigators entering house of criminal

indicators.note: the investigators and the one go into the house, so those letters sit inside the dwelling word

parts.note: a house is a home
one is the Roman numeral I
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: A detective team raids a crook's house and finds someone inside.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is Britain's plain-clothes police branch. 'criminal' is the definition in its rarer sense of a person who kills, not the act.
explanation.definitionFit: The word also names a killer, a person guilty of slaying someone, which is a kind of lawbreaker.

clue.text: 2 takes in work with confidence

indicators.note: the pronoun swallows the work, putting it between its two letters

parts.note: the number points to the answer of clue 2 down, a word for a man, which gives the pronoun HE
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a job with self-assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: A bare number in a clue means the answer to that clue; 2 down's answer is a man, so HE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have trust or expectation that something will turn out well is to feel assured about it.

clue.text: A little mild beer after sex

indicators.note: only a small piece of the word mild is taken, its opening letter

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A drinker has a half of mild once the lovemaking is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Mild is a British dark beer, so 'A little mild beer' reads as one order; in fact 'A little' takes just M from mild.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the two biological sexes, the one that is not female.

clue.text: Company accountant has a good laugh

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
a hoot is something very funny

explanation.surface: A firm's accountant enjoys a bit of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition uses the phrase 'in cahoots', partnership or company.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in league or partnership with someone is keeping close company with them.

clue.text: Wrongly credit this account -it may be necessary to charge

definitions.text: it may be necessary to charge

indicators.note: the letters of credit are wrongly ordered and must be rearranged

parts.note: a current account is an everyday bank account

explanation.surface: A bank warns that an incorrectly credited account may lead to fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a bank fee; it is charging a battery, which needs a steady one-way flow of electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Batteries are recharged with one-way electric flow, so that flow is needed to charge them.

clue.text: Protective wear on board fishing craft

indicators.note: with board read as a ship, being on board puts the raincoat inside the vessel's letters

parts.note: on board means aboard ship, and SS (steamship) is the crossword ship
a mack (mackintosh) is a raincoat worn for protection

explanation.surface: Fishermen pull on oilskins as they climb aboard their boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the old convention for going inside SS, the steamship. A MACK is a British word for a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Small sailing vessels used for fishing, often with a well to keep the catch alive, carry this name.

clue.text: One gropes, lest more should fail

indicators.note: the words lest more fall apart and their letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A warning: someone fumbles, in case more things go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who touches others sexually without consent is one who gropes.

clue.text: Englishman's housekeeper?

parts.note: the saying goes that an Englishman's home is his castle, so the one keeping his house keeps a castle

explanation.surface: A question about who runs an Englishman's home.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'An Englishman's home is his castle' turns a housekeeper into the mistress of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the lady in charge of a castle or large household.

clue.text: Wets are the dearest to convert

indicators.note: the words are converted, changed into a new arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A political jibe: the timid Tory wets are the most precious to win over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wets' were moderate Conservatives in Thatcher's era.
explanation.definitionFit: A loved one or darling is addressed as dearest.

clue.text: Fish and chips fried with lard

indicators.note: cooking in fat churns up the ingredients, so the letters of the two words are mixed

explanation.surface: An order at a seaside chip shop, everything cooked in lard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish and chips' reads as one dish; in fact 'Fish' is the definition and 'chips' joins 'lard' as anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small oily sea fish of the herring family, adult sardines.

clue.text: Previous government meets previous administration

indicators.note: administering is managing and arranging, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The old regime holds talks with the outgoing cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'administration' looks like a government, a second definition; it is the anagram signal for MEETS PREVIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The parliament of the former USSR is a past ruling body, now gone.

clue.text: Part English living in Bath

indicators.note: the English letter takes up residence inside the bathing word

parts.note: to lave is an old word for to bathe or wash

explanation.surface: Some of the English population lives in the spa city of Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath looks like the English spa city; here it is the verb, to wash. 'Part' is a verb too, to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: To depart or go away from a place is to part from it.

clue.text: Smitten English conscience put down to being lustful

indicators.note: a smitten conscience is knocked about, so its letters with those of put are jumbled
the English letter is put down, so it is the one left over when the jumble is made

explanation.surface: A guilty English conscience blames its stricken state on desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smitten' signals the anagram of CONSCIENCE plus PUT; one E (English) is 'down', dropped from that pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a formal, Latinate term for feeling strong sexual desire.

clue.text: Beverage with body doctor takes in the King's Head

parts.note: a stiff is slang for a corpse, a dead body

indicators.note: the head of king is its first letter

explanation.surface: A doctor downs a strong one in a pub called the King's Head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the King's Head' is a common British pub name, but here it only gives K.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong alcoholic drink is a kind of beverage.

clue.text: Meetings to discuss wit in verse form

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so the letters are given a new shape

explanation.surface: Talks are held to discuss how to put humour into poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal question-and-answer sessions, as for a job, are a kind of meeting.

clue.text: Fish that acts like a spanner?

definitions.text: Fish that acts like a spanner?

parts.words: Fish that acts like a spanner?
parts.note: a spanner tightens things up, much as someone adjusting an instrument does, and the fish's name is said like the word for such an adjuster

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about a fish that can be used as a wrench.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish's name is pronounced like 'tuner', one who tightens or adjusts, which is what a spanner does to a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: A large ocean fish of the mackerel family, widely eaten, also called tunny.

clue.text: Tend to fast while one devours treacle pudding

indicators.note: the one swallows the mixed treacle, so those letters go inside

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice

indicators.note: a pudding is a mixture, so the letters of treacle are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A dieter tries to fast while somebody else gobbles a treacle sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pudding' makes CELERAT. 'fast' suggests going without food, but it means speed: to tend toward going faster.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up speed is to move toward greater quickness.

clue.text: A doctor tries unsuccessfully to wipe out …

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: the word tries goes wrong, so its letters come out scrambled

explanation.surface: A doctor's failed attempts to clear a debt carry on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots link this clue to 20 down's surface: 'to wipe out or treat'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay off a debt gradually by instalments is to clear it entirely.

clue.text: Second-hand store swift to grasp a foreign coin

indicators.note: the swift word holds the other letters inside its grip

parts.note: fleet means swift, fast-moving
the mark was the German currency before the euro

explanation.surface: A nimble shopkeeper snaps up a coin from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird 'swift' is a red herring; here it is the adjective, fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: A street market selling cheap used goods is a place to buy second-hand things.

clue.text: Protuberance turns foul

indicators.note: the foul word turns round, so it is read from right to left

parts.note: rank means foul-smelling

explanation.surface: A lump on something goes bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A knar is a knot or bump on a tree trunk, a protruding growth.

clue.text: … or treat, causing hardship

parts.note: to deal with something is to treat it

explanation.surface: Continuing the doctor's story: to eliminate or cure, painful either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful and difficult experience is an ordeal of suffering.

clue.text: Where couples may part and then prepare to wed?

definitions.text: Where couples may part and then prepare to wed?

parts.words: Where couples may part and then prepare to wed?
parts.note: a legal place for ending marriages, with a playful second reading: split up, then woo someone new

explanation.surface: A wry question about where marriages end and new romances begin.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word of the answer is ending a marriage; the second is a law court, but also means to woo, preparing to wed again.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the court that hears cases for ending marriages.

clue.text: Name of girl called Nancy

indicators.note: the name is taken out of the run of words, sitting across two of them

explanation.surface: Identifying a girl whose name is Nancy.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle 'called' and 'Nancy'. 'Name of girl' reads as one phrase but 'of' is the signal for taking letters out.
explanation.definitionFit: Edna is a girl's first name.

clue.text: Revolutionary in wrong revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the wrong word is read backwards

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A rebel is caught up in a misguided uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: A TORT is a legal wrong; backwards it gives a Trotskyist.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Trotsky is a left-wing revolutionary.

clue.text: One nice group of Britons Rome found revolting

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the letters of nice rise up and rearrange themselves

explanation.surface: A tribe of ancient Britons whom the Romans found nasty rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is historical: this tribe, led by Boudicca, revolted against Roman rule. 'Rome found' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribe of ancient Britain in East Anglia, famous for Boudicca's uprising.

clue.text: The last to give thanks to one who makes advances

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
one is the Roman numeral I
a lender is someone who advances money

explanation.surface: Final gratitude is owed to a money-lender or a suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advances' suggests romance, but here it means loans. In cricket, a TAIL-ENDER is one of the weakest batters, who come in last.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes whoever comes at the very end of a line or batting order.

clue.text: King is confronted by fate

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
to meet someone can mean to face or confront them

explanation.surface: A king comes face to face with his destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, from Arabic and Turkish, means destiny or what is preordained.

clue.text: Resolute law-breaker in open confinement

indicators.note: the broken law goes inside the opening word
the opening word holds the other letters confined within it

parts.note: to open something is to start it

indicators.note: the law is broken, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm-minded criminal serving time in an open prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaker' makes ALW. 'law-breaker' reads as a criminal, and 'open confinement' as an open prison, but it is the starting word holding the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone staunch and dependable, firm in purpose, is described with this word.
